title: Greedy vertex coloring with neighbor access

verifiedRecords.quality: Proper vertex coloring from the common palette [Δ+1]
verifiedRecords.output: An explicit color for every vertex; n vertex–color assignments.
verifiedRecords.graph: Undirected simple graph with known labeled vertex set [n], n≥1, m edges, maximum degree Δ.
verifiedRecords.oracle: Neighbor(v,j) returns the j-th neighbor in a fixed arbitrary ordering, or ⊥ when j>d(v).
verifiedRecords.probability: Deterministic; correct on every input satisfying the graph and oracle promises.
verifiedRecords.theorem: §1 query-model definition and greedy baseline; Table 1 and the g(Δ)=nΔ discussion before Corollary 2
verifiedRecords.displayBound: Exactly n+2m neighbor calls for the scan-and-greedy implementation
verifiedRecords.sourceBound: Source baseline O(nΔ) for Δ≥1; the source's O(m) successful-neighbor accounting suppresses end tests/isolated vertices.
verifiedRecords.totalTime: O(n+m) unit-cost RAM time, including oracle calls and explicit output
verifiedRecords.space: O(n) auxiliary words, including the n output colors; adjacency lists need not be retained
derivation: Process vertices in any fixed order. For each v, call Neighbor(v,1), Neighbor(v,2), … until the first ⊥.
The calls returning vertices sum to ∑v d(v)=2m; one terminal call for each vertex contributes n. Thus Q=n+2m exactly for this implementation.
Mark colors already used by previously colored neighbors; choose the smallest unmarked positive color. At most d(v) colors are forbidden, so the choice is at most d(v)+1≤Δ+1.
Use a timestamped color-mark array: marking and finding the first free color cost O(d(v)+1) per vertex. Total RAM time is O(n+m), and O(n) words suffice.
assumptions: All n vertices are known, including isolates; lists are consistent with one simple undirected graph.
The oracle returns ⊥ after the end of each finite list. A padded list that never signals termination is a different model.
No degree or pair queries are used. The implementation does not need Δ in advance.
The exact count describes this full-scan implementation, not every coloring algorithm and not a query lower bound.
When m=0, the scan still makes n end tests and outputs n copies of color 1. For Δ≥1, n+2m≤n(Δ+1)≤2nΔ.
verifiedRecords.notes: The exact scan formula and RAM implementation are elementary atlas derivations from the source's access definition and greedy baseline. They are not a new author-stated optimality theorem. Sparse graphs can have high Δ, so m is retained instead of plotting every instance at n².
